wins: Mapped perimeter network and discovered target host 10.0.0.5 with HTTP (80) and SSH (22) open using nmap fast scan (nmap -sV -T4 10.0.0.5)
Captured web directory listing and identified vulnerable PHP upload endpoint (/upload.php) enabling further file interaction
Gained initial foothold via authenticated file upload followed by reverse shell staging (nc -lvnp 4444)
fails: Privilege escalation stalled after executing linpeas.sh; no misconfigurations or weak sudo rules were exploitable
Post-compromise persistence attempts failed because cron binary was restricted and no writable init scripts were available
Data exfiltration could not be completed due to outbound firewall blocking on port 443 from the compromised host
key_outcomes.summary: Strong initial reconnaissance and initial access but stalled in lateral movement and persistence phases; need to improve privilege escalation and data egress techniques.

repeated_failure_patterns.pattern: Privilege escalation attempts relying solely on linpeas output without cross-verifying sudo rights or kernel exploits
Outbound tunneling blocked when attempting HTTPS exfiltration via curl due to egress filtering

skill_cards.if_condition: When port 22 is open and SSH banner indicates OpenSSH
skill_cards.then_action: Run targeted SSH enumeration with nmap scripts and bruteforce checks

skill_cards.if_condition: When HTTP 80 returns /upload.php with writable temp directory
skill_cards.then_action: Leverage PHP file upload to deploy reverse shell and pivot to netcat listener

skill_cards.if_condition: When outbound traffic is blocked on TCP 443 from compromised host
skill_cards.then_action: Establish SOCKS proxy via SSH agent tunneling or use DNS tunnel tool (iodine)

memory_ops.reason: Consistent success discovering SSH configuration details in early reconnaissance
Reliable initial access via file upload confirmed

next_experiments.title: Kernel exploit verification
next_experiments.description: Run automated kernel exploit scanners (e.g., searchsploit, linux-exploit-suggester) against /proc/version and kernel release to find privilege escalation vectors beyond linpeas output

next_experiments.title: Alternative persistence paths
next_experiments.description: Explore writable cron.d entries and systemd timers via find /etc -perm -4000 -ls to identify unexpected persistence hooks

next_experiments.title: Data exfiltration via DNS tunnel
next_experiments.description: Attempt outbound data transfer using iodine with domain fronting to bypass port 443 restrictions
